text:
sara: quick RFC follow-up — we need a lightweight handshake for per-tenant precision overrides. customers want to pin fp8 for cost, but ops needs automatic rollback to int8/4bit on quality regressions. how do we express this at the routing layer without exploding config complexity?

kevin: +1. thinking a two-phase contract: (1) static override (customer preference) and (2) runtime safety gates (degscore + tokenwise regression). routing checks both before selecting model variant. keep the schema minimal.

leo: proposal: an ordered list with fallback tiers, e.g. [fp8, int8, int4] plus a small set of triggers: deg_threshold, latency_budget_ms, canary_sample_rate. then runtime can pick highest-ranked variant that satisfies triggers.

priya: we also need telemetry predicates — e.g., who owns the degscore calculation? ops wants it normalized per-customer because prompt distributions differ. suggestion: expose quality_signal_namespace and let customers opt into a local baseline.

kevin: agree. sketch of route block: 

route: /generate/chat
precision_overrides:
  tenant_override: [fp8, int8, int4]
  safety_gates:
    deg_threshold: 0.15
    latency_budget_ms: 120
    canary_sample_rate: 0.02
  quality_signal_namespace: tenant_abc

sara: nice. two operational concerns: 1) prefix/KV cache compatibility when switching between precisions mid-conversation, 2) rollback semantics for in-flight requests. both can cause user-facing glitchiness.

leo: for KV cache, we should require a compatible_cache_profile flag on the override. if false, runtime must flush prefix cache on precision switch and accept the latency hit for first request. if true, allow switch without flush. default: false.

priya: rollback semantics: do graceful fallback for new incoming requests only. in-flight tokens continue on the original variant to avoid partial-response mismatch. that keeps behavior deterministic.

kevin: ops-bot thought: @ops-bot can we run a sampling job to estimate the cache-flush penalty across recent customer workloads and attach percentiles?

ops-bot: scheduled sample-run for tenant_abc at 2026-04-02T08:00Z. results posted to /eng-ml/precision-observability later today. :white_check_mark:

sara: one more tradeoff — complexity of the API surface. do we shove all of this into route config, or provide a separate precision_policy object referenced by route id?

leo: separate object wins for reuse. customers with many endpoints will thank us. also allows safer rollout: change policy reference to switch behavior across many routes atomically.

priya: ops concerns about defaults: we should ship a conservative default policy (favor quality, low canary sample) and an "aggressive cost" preset for self-serve. also require enterprise consent for auto-rollbacks that could alter output semantics.

kevin: agreed. implementation plan: - API: add precision_policy_id on route (optional) - DB: store policy versions, pluggable canary config - Runtime: check policy on request, evaluate safety gates, and consult cache_compat flag before switching - Observability: emit precision_decision event with reason, selected_variant, and fallback_history

sara: leaves action items: 1) leo: draft precision_policy schema (include variant_list, safety_gates, cache_compat, quality_namespace, rollout_rules) — due EOD tomorrow 2) kevin: prototype runtime decision path in toy harness (simulate switching, flush cost) — due next Tue 3) priya: write ops playbook for canary rollback and customer notification text — due next Wed 4) ops-bot: run sampling job and post results — ETA today

priya: also capture legal/compliance: if a tenant pins a precision that reduces quality (e.g., hallucination rate), we need a signoff flow for enterprise customers. adding to playbook.

leo: quick question — do we allow per-call override via SDK header, or only per-route/policy? per-call is powerful but dangerous.

kevin: prefer not to enable per-call by default. if we do, require precision_policy to declare allow_per_call: true and we audit any per-call changes.

sara: sounds good. last note — add a lightweight evaluation harness to nightly checks: shadow fp8 paths and compute delta vs baseline to catch regressions before customers opt in. that should reduce surprises.

priya: +1. ok I'm good with the action items. thanks all :rocket:
